newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BMW, Chrysler in Brazil venture.
newsitem.headline: BMW, Chrysler in Brazil venture.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG said it has formed a joint venture with Chrysler Corp to build a $500 million motor plant in Brazil by 1999, and its local unit plans to build a $150 million Land Rover assembly plant, an official said.
"BMW group and Chrysler have decided to build an engine factory together and this plant will definitely be in Brazil," Michael Turwitt, BMW do Brasil Ltda president, told reporters.
BMW's local unit also plans to build a $150 million car plant in Brazil to assemble up to 15,000 Land Rover Defenders by 1998 through completely knocked-down production, he added.
Part of the assembly plant's production will be exported to Mercosur partners Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, he added.
Turwitt said BMW and Chrysler each would invest $250 million in the engine plant, which would produce 400,000 engines yearly and generate 3,000 jobs, directly and indirectly.

The plant would produce late-model 1.4 and 1.6-liter engines, which would be exported to Asia and Europe and also be used in the production of Chrysler's compact vehicles and BMW's Rover cars, he said.

He said the companies have not decided yet precisely where in Brazil the engine and auto assembly plants will be located but added they would be built in Brazil's southern or southeastern. "We expect to announce locations for the plants in the first quarter this year," Turwitt said.
BMW also has plans to import Rover 200s and other vehicles from the Rover family to Brazil, he said.

BMW and Chrysler are among newcomers such as Renault SA, Daimler-Benz AG, Honda Motor Co Ltd, Toyota Motor Corp and Asia Motors Co Ltd, which announced last year plans to set up plants in the country.
